A new work-practice policy is appended to every system prompt, ensuring the agent implements the requested approach exactly, keeps scratch out of the repo, and scales verification to the change size. This applies to all runs, not just benchmarks.

title.en: Streaming performance: coalesced deltas and per-block Markdown parsing

body.en: Streaming deltas are now coalesced before reaching the frontend, reducing IPC overhead. Markdown is parsed per completed block instead of per tick, cutting parse count dramatically for typical answers. Frame deltas are folded into one reducer pass per tab, lowering UI thread load.

title.en: File tools now route through FileOverlay and writes are atomic

body.en: All file-editing tools (edit_file, multi_edit, delete_range, etc.) now respect the host FileOverlay, preventing overwrites of unsaved editor buffers. File writes are atomic, using temp-file-and-rename to avoid corruption on crash.

title.en: Sandbox detection probes usability, not just PATH presence

body.en: On macOS, sandbox-exec availability is now probed with a minimal profile, correctly reporting unavailability on restricted systems where it exists but cannot apply sandboxing. This prevents silent enforcement failures.

body.en: Stuck in-app updates now self-heal: stale probationary updates auto-commit after 24h, version comparison normalizes leading 'v', and a new 'Discard previous update' button allows manual recovery. Recovery docs updated.

title.en: Prevent stale results after reasoning-only stops

body.en: Internal consumers like sub-agents and planners now require a visible final answer. Reasoning-only stops trigger a bounded retry, and cleanup is compaction-aware, preserving completed evidence. Guardian reviews fail closed after empty finals.

title.en: Windows POSIX hook scripts normalized across sources

body.en: POSIX shebang scripts from plugins, projects, and global hooks on Windows are now detected and routed through Git Bash. Paths are normalized, and Bash dependencies are visible to diagnostics.

title.en: UI latency telemetry with performance budgets

body.en: Desktop now records UI latency metrics (frame duration, input latency, markdown parse time, etc.) via anonymous counters, with documented performance budgets. No message content is collected.

title.en: Per-task trajectory recording and wall-time attribution

body.en: The CLI and benchmark harness can now record per-task event trajectories (--trajectory) and attribute wall time to tools vs. model thinking. Reports include time attribution when trajectories are recorded.

title.en: Tool result timestamps for time attribution

body.en: Tool results now carry absolute start/end timestamps, enabling reconstruction of where a turn's time went. Cancelled or skipped calls carry zero timestamps.

body.en: Function size and complexity are now gated in CI. File-size ceiling extended to TypeScript. All build tags are linted across platforms. Modern Go idioms adopted and enforced.

Per-tab model switches are serialized, stale balance and catalog responses are discarded, failed switches restore safe state, and session-local picks no longer rewrite the global default for new sessions.
Periodic parent refreshes no longer refocus the revision editor and clear transcript text that the user selected for copying.

title.en: Documentation sidebar tracks the active section

body.en: The documentation site now highlights the section that is actually visible instead of leaving a stale sidebar item active.

title.en: One-time bootstrap for existing Debian packages

body.en: Older .deb installs do not contain the new Polkit helper. Install the 1.17.20 .deb once with sudo apt install ./Patty Code-linux-amd64.deb; later in-app updates can use the authorized helper without uninstalling first.

title.en: Keep Desktop and Remote hosts on matching versions

body.en: The remote protocol adds optional resolved-capability metadata. Old data remains readable, but Desktop and Remote hosts should follow the existing matching-build upgrade contract.

Existing providers, sessions, projects, Goals, jobs, and MCP definitions continue to load. The events-jsonl machine interface creates a private per-install identity key on first use; legacy json and stream-json resume identifiers remain unchanged.

title.en: Installed MCP authorization is the trust boundary

body.en: Planner and ordinary sub-agents can call installed and authorized MCP capabilities without another launch prompt. Explicit deny rules, live revocation, destructive checks, exact runtime identity, and serialized writer dispatch still apply.

title.en: Zero-config MCPs, reliable Todos, and a sharper desktop

summary.en: This release makes trusted MCP servers connect reliably with less setup, keeps Todo progress authoritative across local and remote sessions, improves workspace navigation and selected-context previews, and hardens Auto decisions, configuration persistence, registry review, and Windows packaging.

body.en: Review the updated Auto behavior and the decisions that still require explicit user input.

title.en: Trusted MCP servers work with less setup

body.en: Installed and authorized MCP servers now register cached tools immediately, start on demand, expose clearer runtime state, and shut down without leaving schema-cache writes behind.
The Desktop Todo panel now follows canonical server state across completion, resume, rewind, session switches, and Remote Workbench snapshots instead of reviving stale transcript data.
The file tree remembers useful expansion state, compacts directory chains, adds Seti file icons and nesting guides, while selected chat or code context remains visible as an expandable message card.

title.en: Auto asks only at real plan boundaries

body.en: Routine allowed work continues automatically, while genuine strategy or scope transitions receive a neutral plan comparison across Desktop, CLI, and bot clients.

title.en: Plugin submissions in the community registry

body.en: Publishers can submit plugin packages alongside skills and MCP servers, with validated metadata and install routing.
Selected chat excerpts and code added to a prompt remain visible and expandable after sending without duplicating model-visible context.

Quick install, manual setup, and JSON setup now share one flow; enable, disable, retry, child-agent inheritance, startup single-flight, project-relative commands, and cleanup follow consistent host-side rules.
Expansion memory, compact directory chains, nesting guides, and bundled Seti icons make large workspaces easier to scan on macOS and Windows.
Save actions, keyboard focus, Escape handling, busy state, and narrow-window layout now behave consistently inside Settings.
Publisher updates return to review, clear stale verification, and require approval against the exact revision so concurrent changes fail closed.
MiniMax review failures now preserve upstream diagnostics and explain that the full conversation context may be involved instead of suggesting an ineffective retry.

title.en: ACP command availability after session startup

body.en: Command updates are now sent only after new, loaded, or resumed session responses, so clients can register before notifications arrive.

title.en: Permission edits preserve the full policy

body.en: Remembering a new allow rule no longer drops mode, ask, deny, comments, or unknown permission fields, and concurrent writers are serialized across processes.

title.en: Windows portable packages keep the GUI launcher

body.en: The bundled CLI now uses a distinct internal filename, preventing case-insensitive staging from replacing Patty Code.exe with the console executable.

title.en: Todo panels no longer revive completed work

body.en: Canonical Todo snapshots now win over transcript reconstruction, including authoritative empty lists and guarded asynchronous refreshes.

Existing providers, sessions, projects, and MCP definitions continue to load. MCP enable and disable choices are stored in a new separate activation file when changed; a missing file preserves legacy auto_start behavior.

title.en: Remote Workbench, Auto Guard, and a smoother desktop

summary.en: This release adds a Windows-to-Linux Remote Workbench powered by local providers, strengthens Auto mode with Auto Guard, simplifies installed MCP authorization, and improves file previews, onboarding, updates, and session safety.

body.en: Connect the desktop client to a Linux SSH host while keeping model access on the local machine.
Understand the approval choices used by local and remote workflows.
Use the Windows desktop client against a Linux workspace while the local provider broker keeps model credentials and inference on the client machine.
Auto mode now evaluates recovery decisions more deliberately and records enough context to keep interrupted work moving safely.
Installed MCP servers now follow a clearer trust and authorization path without the retired catalog workflow.
Desktop file previews now include line numbers and in-file search for faster navigation through source and text files.
Added SSH host discovery, trust prompts, remote runtime attachment, file and Git projections, reconnect handling, and local-provider brokering for Remote Workbench.
Added deterministic recovery rules, review records, and guarded continuation for Auto mode.
Added a dedicated large-file preview component with line numbers, text search, and keyboard navigation.
The first-run experience now leads users into provider setup with clearer choices and status feedback.
Windows updates now show progress and use a hardened handoff and startup-recovery path when an update is interrupted.
MCP packages and servers now use the installed registry and an explicit trust dialog instead of the former signed catalog path.
Project documentation and the website now expose direct installation paths for the Patty Code VS Code extension.
Archive actions now reject the active session and active topic, preventing a live conversation from disappearing underneath its runtime.
Release-blocking SSH lifecycle, reconnect, provider-catalog, and shutdown cleanup defects found during physical Windows-to-Linux acceptance have been fixed.
Existing local workspaces, providers, and desktop preferences continue to load normally. Remote Workbench is opt-in and requires a reachable OpenSSH-compatible Linux host.

summary.en: This release brings ACP mid-turn steering, workspace diffs in Changes, retirement of automatic Plan Mode, and various UI and lifecycle fixes.

Details on configuration file locations.

Technical specification.

AutoResearch now requires an explicit Goal selection or `/goal` command, preventing accidental research activation.
Support for the `_patty.io/session/steer` ACP vendor extension, allowing clients to guide active sessions.
Added a read-only API to show the complete Git HEAD-to-worktree diff with syntax highlighting and line numbers.
Automatic Plan Mode has been retired; planning now requires explicit manual activation. Existing configurations are automatically migrated.
AutoResearch is now only available after an explicit Goal selection or `/goal` command, removing the automatic classifier and preventing unintended activation.

title.en: Controller cancels foreground work on close

body.en: Fixed a lifecycle defect where `Controller.Close()` would not cancel active foreground contexts or pending waiters, potentially leaving orphaned operations and false idle states.
Fixed CSS grid layout so that model option cards no longer visually overlap when providers have many models or long names.

title.en: Windows opener menu now stays above transcript

body.en: Fixed an issue where the external-opener menu on Windows could be hidden behind conversation content.

title.en: CC Switch MCP import respects enabled_patty

body.en: MCP servers from CC Switch are now correctly imported using the `enabled_patty` flag, with compatible fallbacks for older schemas.

title.en: WebView2 startup isolated from system proxies

body.en: WebView2 shell starts without proxy to avoid stalling on unreachable proxies, with a 15-second watchdog and recovery prompt.

title.en: Remote SSH config aligned with OpenSSH

body.en: SSH connection resolution now uses the full OpenSSH configuration stack and aligns authentication behavior, including IdentityFile and IdentitiesOnly handling.
Fixed virtual row overlap in the file tree after directory expansion by using stable file paths as keys.

Automatic Plan Mode has been removed. Your configuration will be automatically migrated on first launch: `auto_plan` will be set to off and legacy keys removed. Planning must now be started explicitly (e.g., via Shift+Tab).

summary.en: Remote SSH and parallel subagent fleets lead this release, alongside regional typography, customizable composer shortcuts, reliable exports, and stronger session and MCP recovery.

body.en: Configure hosts, connect from the CLI or Desktop, browse remote files, and manage forwarded ports.
Chinese guide for Remote SSH host setup, connections, files, and port forwarding.
Learn how to define and use subagent profiles, configure fleets, and manage concurrency.
Customize pane opacity and explore theme pack authoring.
See the latest CLI features, including middle-click paste and improved transcript layout.
Connect to a remote host over SSH and run the full Patty Code agent and tools remotely. Includes host manager, file browser, port forwarding, and automatic reconnection.
Run up to 64 independent subagent tasks in parallel with configurable concurrency and profile-based system prompts. Safe write-path coordination prevents conflicts.
Independently adjust font family and size for interface, conversation, composer, and code areas with live preview.
Streamlined MCP server installation and tool approval. Direct add-and-connect flow, per-project launch grants, and removed legacy trust management.
Image and PDF exports now work reliably across all platforms, with large conversations automatically split into multiple files.
Full VS Code Remote‑SSH style experience: connect to a remote host, run the agent there, browse and edit files, forward ports, and reconnect automatically.
Parallel subagent execution with profiles, concurrency limits, write-path coordination, and background task support.
Set a custom context window for individual models behind a shared provider endpoint.
Configure separate shortcuts for sending a message and inserting a newline in the composer.
Restore middle-click paste in the Patty Code CLI (tmux buffer or PRIMARY selection).
Fine-tune fonts and sizes for different parts of the UI: interface, conversation, composer, and code/tools.
Choose between Standard (960px) and Full width (90%) for the chat area.
Added pane opacity controls for home/workspace scenes; fixed active theme reverting on settings save.
Removed legacy trust state machine; user‑added servers now connect directly, and tool approval respects explicit install authorization.
Imported skills now correctly map to live MCP tools even when they use raw or upstream names.
Separated release crashes from development signals; reduced spurious prompts; fixed virtualizer and Mermaid rendering errors.
Better copy/paste handling, restored right-click paste, and improved transcript layout and spacing.
Fixed cross‑origin canvas taint and memory issues; exports now work everywhere and auto‑split long conversations.
Cancelled or errored turns now keep their visible output in the UI across tab switches and reloads.
Session save now times out after 5 seconds instead of hanging, preserving a recovery branch on shutdown.
Correctly invoke .bat/.cmd plugins with quoted paths on Windows.
Custom provider names starting with a digit now generate valid environment variable names.
Servers with multiple valid host keys no longer cause false mismatch errors.
Connection errors now appear in the status popover with retry and host management actions.
Prevent crashes on Linux by reapplying signal handler flags during WebKit startup.
Cursor no longer stays as a resize handle when the desktop window is maximized.
Corrected the preset to the official 1,048,576‑token limit, delaying premature compaction.
Replaced reserved characters like colon with hyphen when creating session files.
Fixed the publish CTA in the registry toolbar rendering as a narrow pill.
The legacy trust state machine has been replaced with per‑project launch grants. Existing MCP servers continue to work; manual trust management options have been removed.
Remote SSH V1 supports Linux and macOS remote hosts. Windows remote hosts are not yet supported and return a clear error.
The new fleet tool and extended task schema intentionally cause one prompt-cache cold start after upgrading. Tool order and schemas remain stable afterward.

summary.en: This release adds the new official Desktop theme experience, makes long-running chats and session switching more reliable, restores persistent MCP sessions, and polishes the CLI workflow.

title.en: Official themes and Theme Pack V2

body.en: Desktop now ships eight official themes, a unified gallery, reversible previews, and a custom editor with independent light, dark, home, and workspace scenes.

title.en: Long runs and session switching stay responsive

body.en: Stalled proxy error bodies no longer freeze retries, while faster session snapshots and stale-activation guards prevent switch lag and content loss.
Compatible trust receipts migrate safely, stdio servers reuse one process across calls, and Desktop provides a direct re-verification path when server identity changes.
The composer scrolls long drafts, clipboard actions distinguish text from images, the status footer adapts to narrow terminals, and model selection completes reliably.
The retired Memory v5 execution compiler is removed, and DeepSeek reasoning-only completions that explicitly stop no longer trigger unnecessary extra thinking rounds.
Added eight bundled themes, six semantic base styles, a theme gallery, a custom editor, and hardened Theme Pack V2 import/export.
patty-code.io now supports system, light, and dark themes, uses the prefix-cache block as a shared visual motif, and presents frequent patch releases in a compact changelog layout.

title.en: Responsive CLI composer and status footer

body.en: Long drafts scroll inside the composer, copy and paste report clearer outcomes, and complete status groups reflow instead of clipping on narrow terminals.
Reloaded user messages recover their original send time, while project search, session search, and Trash replace the duplicated standalone History entry.
CLI, npm, and Desktop stable publishers now validate one atomic tag set and fan out after a single protected GitHub approval.

title.en: Retry freezes and session-switch data loss

body.en: Non-responsive error bodies are bounded, no-op snapshots avoid repeated rewrites, and out-of-order Desktop activations can no longer replace the most recently selected session.
Compatible trust state migrates, authorized servers connect without duplicate prompts, stdio sessions persist across calls, and identity drift exposes a dedicated re-verification action.

title.en: Model switching from the quick picker

body.en: Choosing a model or provider from the CLI picker now starts and completes the controller switch instead of leaving input permanently blocked.
A non-empty reasoning stream ending with finish_reason=stop is accepted as complete instead of triggering up to three unnecessary retries.
Secret-shaped identifiers in code, tool output, transcripts, recovery branches, and job artifacts are no longer rewritten by heuristic redaction.

title.en: Windows external openers and workspace preference

body.en: Desktop discovers App Paths installations, launches shells without reparsing metacharacters, chooses renderable terminal icons, and restores the workspace panel's open state.
No manual migration is required. A stale [agent].memory_compiler setting is removed once during startup, while legacy transcripts and citations remain readable.
Ordinary model and tool content is now stored verbatim in private local files. If a tool prints a real credential, run patcode doctor redact-sessions or review the files before sharing them.
A persistent stdio server uses its normal writer sandbox for all RPCs. Plan-mode filtering, tool policy, explicit deny rules, and destructive-action approval still apply at dispatch time.

summary.en: This release improves the desktop experience with clearer MCP error messages, Windows plugin hook fixes, executable icons, and a new bilingual changelog.

How to create, configure, and distribute Patty Code plugins.
Chinese guide for creating, configuring, and distributing Patty Code plugins.
How to build, validate, and publish a Patty Code release.
Release notes are now reviewed and published in English and Chinese, with dedicated version pages. Desktop update banners link directly to the matching release.
MCP connection failures now show the registry host and endpoint in the error summary, helping to diagnose proxy or network issues.
Plugin hooks on Windows now correctly expand aliases like ${REASONIX_PLUGIN_ROOT}, support bash hooks, and handle non-UTF-8 output.
Windows launcher, guard, and updater now display the Patty Code icon and include version metadata.
Manual desktop updates now open the Desktop download page with the correct OS highlighted.
Added a reviewed, versioned bilingual release catalog; website now has changelog and version pages linking from desktop update banners.
Launcher, guard, and update helper now have the Patty Code icon and version metadata.
MCP error summaries now show the npm registry host and endpoint for connection failures.
Plugin hooks on Windows now expand aliases, work with bash, and handle legacy encodings.
Manual updates now open the Desktop download page with OS highlighted.

title.en: A safer delivery loop, trusted MCP execution, and offline recovery

summary.en: This release makes long-running work safer from planning through delivery. It adds an offline recovery Guard and Safe Mode, hardens MCP package identity and credentials, improves Claude plugin compatibility, and polishes the desktop and CLI workflows used every day.

body.en: Use patty-code-guard to diagnose configuration and installation failures, restore a snapshot, or start in Safe Mode.
Learn how plugin packages bundle skills, hooks, and MCP servers while preserving explicit trust boundaries.
A recovery path now exists outside the normal desktop startup. It can inspect failures, restore known-good state, and launch a minimal Safe Mode when normal boot is blocked.
User-installed MCP servers work immediately. Repository-declared servers still require one exact identity approval before startup, and identity changes invalidate that approval.

title.en: Delivery that recovers instead of cascading

body.en: Goal, Plan, Delivery, YOLO, and review readiness now share a consistent lifecycle. Interrupted delivery can recover without concurrent writers corrupting the final state.
Patty Code can consume Claude-compatible plugin packages and adapt their commands and hooks into the existing plugin runtime.
Pinned conversations get their own section, selected chat text or workspace code can be sent to the composer, and files can open through a dynamically discovered external-app menu.

title.en: Mouse selection in the CLI composer

body.en: Text in the terminal composer can now be selected with the mouse.

title.en: Pinned conversations in the classic sidebar

body.en: Pinned topics stay visible in a dedicated section instead of being mixed into recency sorting.
Bounded edit receipts keep the agent grounded while avoiding redundant full-file reads.
Sorting, previews, topic actions, tab boundaries, and draggable whitespace now behave more consistently.
A pending plan approval no longer disappears after moving between sessions.
Shell-escaped paths, mixed-DPI restore, and long isolated checkout paths are handled safely.
All persisted credential environment keys are isolated from unrelated providers and subprocesses.

If you previously selected the retired native Windows sandbox, open Settings → Sandbox after upgrading and choose a supported isolation mode. Patty Code reports a remediation message instead of silently falling back.

title.en: MCP trust may require fresh approval

body.en: When a package identity or executable no longer matches its stored receipt, Patty Code asks for a new approval rather than reusing stale trust.
The MCP and read-only subagent changes fail closed. Invalid schemas, identities, or receipts are quarantined or returned to human approval instead of being accepted automatically.

title.en: Provider setup becomes a real control center

summary.en: Provider setup now works as a complete manager instead of a one-time wizard. Delivery review and liveness checks are stricter, while the Creation workspace, performance diagnostics, and everyday desktop interactions receive focused polish.

body.en: Add, edit, test, and choose provider access from one terminal workflow instead of rerunning a first-use wizard.
Delivery mode now aligns review protocol, readiness gates, sign-off evidence, and streaming liveness.
Desktop performance prompts use JavaScript self-profiling attribution and suppress false positives during recovery.
The changes view, sidebar alignment, dock geometry, chat scrollbar, and text scaling now follow one visual system.
A manually resized composer no longer collapses to a single visible line.
The desktop cache summary updates with the active session instead of showing stale averages.
Existing providers and desktop preferences continue to load unchanged.

title.en: Runtime profiles, plugin commands, and safer session handoffs

summary.en: This release introduces configurable subagent and runtime profiles, maps Claude plugin commands into Patty Code, and closes several session handoff gaps that could hide messages, drop turns, or obscure provider failures.

body.en: Create isolated subagent profiles with their own instructions, models, and capability boundaries.
Work modes can select the runtime profile and delivery capabilities appropriate to the task.
Claude-compatible plugin commands and skills appear as qualified custom slash commands without name collisions.
402, 429, 5xx, 401, and 403 responses now surface the upstream reason instead of a generic failure.

title.en: Turns are not dropped during finish

body.en: Messages submitted while a turn is finishing are parked and resumed instead of silently disappearing.
Missing capability arrays no longer crash the diagnostics page.
Runtime profiles and plugin command qualification preserve existing configuration.
